Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Senses naturally experience attraction and aversion toward environmental objects. However, one must not fall under the control of these dual forces, as attachment and repulsion act as major obstacles on the path of self-mastery.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Managing the volatile dualities of attraction (raga) and aversion (dvesha) triggered by sensory experiences.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna explains that sensory likes and dislikes are automatic bodily responses, but warns against becoming controlled by them. Regulation prevents attachment and aversion from sabotaging peace of mind.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns to regulate sensory triggers so they no longer dictate his choices or emotional state.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Navigating Impulse Control: Resisting automatic urges of attraction or avoidance
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Equanimity over Polarization: Staying balanced instead of swinging between intense craving and hatred
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Emotional Regulation: Managing internal reactions to external stimuli calmly

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Indriyasyendriyasyarthe raga-dvesau vyavasthitau (Attraction and aversion naturally exist between senses and objects)
Tayor na vasam agacchet (Do not fall under the control of attraction and aversion)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Attraction (raga) and aversion (dvesha) naturally arise when senses contact sense objects. A seeker must not come under the sway of these dualities, as they are obstacles on the path of self-realization.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Craving things you like and fleeing things you dislike creates an emotional rollercoaster. Recognizing that attraction and aversion are temporary neural responses enables you to make conscious, rational decisions rather than reacting impulsively.
